# braintrust_view (Resource)

Manages a Braintrust saved view or monitor dashboard. A dashboard is a view with `view_type = "monitor"`; its charts are stored in `view_data_json.custom_charts` and share the view lifecycle. JSON values must be objects. Braintrust deep-merges `options_json` on PATCH, so removing an existing option key requires replacing the view.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A saved project-log view and a dashboard with SQL charts share the same API resource.
resource "braintrust_project" "app" {
  name = "my-ml-project"
}

resource "braintrust_view" "errors" {
  object_type = "project"
  object_id   = braintrust_project.app.id
  view_type   = "logs"
  name        = "Error traces"

  view_data_json = jsonencode({
    search = { filter = [] }
  })
}

resource "braintrust_view" "health" {
  object_type = "project"
  object_id   = braintrust_project.app.id
  view_type   = "monitor"
  name        = "Project health"

  options_json = jsonencode({
    viewType = "monitor"
    # type and projectId are needed for the dashboard to appear in the project's
    # Dashboards list.
    options = {
      type       = "project"
      projectId  = braintrust_project.app.id
      spanType   = "range"
      rangeValue = "7d"
    }
  })
  view_data_json = jsonencode({
    custom_charts = {
      version = "0.0.0"
      # Chart IDs are keys in charts; layout.order controls their display order.
      layout = { type = "linear", order = ["spans", "latency_by_model", "note"] }
      charts = {
        spans = {
          title = "Total spans"
          # The project-scoped dashboard supplies the project to project_logs().
          chartSql = "SELECT count(1) AS spans FROM project_logs()"
          viz      = { type = "singleValue", unitType = "count" }
        }
        latency_by_model = {
          title = "Average latency over time by model"
          # Timeseries charts add time bucketing and the dashboard time range.
          # Select each series label and aggregate, then GROUP BY the label.
          chartSql = <<-SQL
            SELECT
              metadata.model AS model,
              avg(metrics.duration) AS avg_duration
            FROM project_logs()
            WHERE metadata.model IS NOT NULL
            GROUP BY model
          SQL
          columnOptions = {
            model        = { displayName = "Model" }
            avg_duration = { displayName = "Average latency" }
          }
          viz = {
            type              = "timeseries"
            timeseriesVizType = "lines"
            unitType          = "duration"
            targetInterval    = "day"
          }
        }
        note = { type = "note", markdown = "## Project health" }
      }
    }
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the view.
- `object_id` (String) ID of the containing object. For org_project dashboards, this is the organization ID; set options_json.options.projectId to the project ID.
- `object_type` (String) Type of the containing object, commonly project or org_project.
- `view_type` (String) Braintrust view type. Use monitor for dashboards or logs for saved project log views.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the view.
- `options_json` (String) JSON object with app view options. Monitor dashboards use viewType=monitor and a nested options object. Existing keys cannot be removed by PATCH; replace the view to remove one.
- `starred` (Boolean) Whether the view is starred in the project.
- `view_data_json` (String) JSON object containing search and/or custom_charts. custom_charts requires a version (currently 0.0.0), and may contain charts, groups, and layout.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) Date of creation.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the view (UUID).
- `updated_at` (String) Date of last update.
- `user_id` (String) Creator's user ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with object_type/object_id/view_id. Braintrust needs the containing object to read a view.
terraform import braintrust_view.example project/<project_id>/<view_id>
```
